name: iam:PassRole + ecs:StartTask
description: Override an existing ECS task definition's container command and task role via ecs:StartTask --overrides on an EC2 container instance to execute code with the passed role's permissions
author: Seth Art

required.description: Must cover both the task role ARN (for the override) and the execution role ARN defined in the existing task definition
Must have permission to start tasks on an existing EC2 container instance in the target cluster

additional.description: Retrieve container instance ARN needed for StartTask
Discover existing task definitions to exploit with overrides

admin: An ECS cluster must exist with at least one registered EC2 container instance
An existing task definition must be available in the cluster
A role must exist that trusts ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com with administrative permissions
lateral: An ECS cluster must exist with at least one registered EC2 container instance
An existing task definition must be available in the cluster
A role must exist that trusts ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com

references.title: Weaponizing AWS ECS Task Definitions to Steal Credentials From Running Containers

options.name: ROLE_ARN
options.description: Target IAM role ARN to pass as the task role override (must trust ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com)

options.name: CLUSTER_NAME
options.description: ECS cluster name or ARN containing the EC2 container instance

options.name: CONTAINER_INSTANCE_ARN
options.description: ARN of the EC2 container instance to start the task on

options.name: TASK_DEFINITION
options.description: Existing task definition family name or ARN to override (no ecs:RegisterTaskDefinition needed)

options.name: CONTAINER_NAME
options.description: Name of the container in the task definition whose command will be overridden (auto-discovered from task definition if not set)

payloads.name: backdoor/attach-policy
payloads.description: Attach AdministratorAccess policy to an IAM user or role via ECS task container command
